faqs.question: What should a Halloween sign say?
faqs.answer: Match the saying to the sign: 2 to 4 words for a yard sign, 3 to 6 for a door hanger and 6 to 12 for a porch board read from the steps. Short jokes like "Coven meeting in progress" work on a door, while a porch board can carry a full sentence.

faqs.question: How big should the letters be on a Halloween yard sign?
faqs.answer: The US highway manual's minimum is 1 inch of letter height per 30 feet, so about 1 1/3 inches for a sign read from 40 feet. For a sign people should read at a glance, aim for 4 to 5 inch capitals, which is what the ADA's 1/8 inch per foot step gives at that distance.

faqs.question: How many words should go on a Halloween door hanger?
faqs.answer: Three to six words is the comfortable range, because a door hanger is read from about 3 feet by someone waiting for the door to open. Letters 5/8 inch tall, the ADA minimum for close eye-level signs, are enough.

faqs.question: What colours are easiest to read on a Halloween sign at night?
faqs.answer: Yellow, white or pumpkin orange on black score highest, from about 7.8:1 to 15:1 on the WCAG contrast formula. Red on black and purple on black come out near 3:1 and 2.3:1, so use them for borders rather than words.

faqs.question: Is a dripping or spooky font OK on a sign?
faqs.answer: Use it for one big word at most. The 2010 ADA Standards exclude script, italic and highly decorative lettering from accessible signs because they are harder to read, and the effect gets worse with distance and low light.

faqs.question: How do I stop a chalkboard sign washing off in the rain?
faqs.answer: Keep chalk lines under a porch roof or behind a window, because rain rinses chalk away. For an exposed spot, paint the letters on wood and seal them with a clear matte outdoor varnish.

faqs.question: How do I light a Halloween sign so people can read it after dark?
faqs.answer: Aim a battery LED spotlight at the sign's face rather than relying on a street lamp; the highway manual itself says street lighting does not count as lighting a sign. Use matte paint so the light does not glare off the letters.

faqs.question: What can I write on a candy bowl sign?
faqs.answer: Make the number the biggest thing on the card, as in "Take two. The skeleton is counting." A short line in 5/8-inch letters is enough, because it is read from 2 to 3 feet.

faqs.question: Are scary warning signs OK on a path where little kids walk?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the real instructions are separate and plain. Put "Exit" and step warnings on their own sign in clear letters, and stake joke signs beside the path, never on it.

faqs.question: Can I put a Halloween sign on my lawn if I rent?
faqs.answer: Check your lease or HOA rules first, because some limit what goes on lawns, doors or shared corridors. A window letter board or a sign inside the door glass is usually the safer choice.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Sayings for Signs, Sized for How Far Away They're Read

The best Halloween sayings for signs fit their length to the distance they are read from: 2 to 4 words for a yard sign seen from the street, 3 to 6 for a door hanger, and 6 to 12 for a porch board read from the steps. Letter height follows the same logic, and the US highway sign manual's ratio of 1 inch of letter height per 30 feet is a floor, not a target. A sign gets one glance per passer-by, whereas a SubhSandesh page sent to one person averages 11.1 views, 48.4% of them on a touch device, so the jobs need different words.

Below are 44 original sayings sorted by sign type, a letter-size table, contrast ratios for common Halloween colour pairs, and how to keep a sign dry until 1 November. The night itself is a Saturday in 2026 (31 October) and a Sunday in 2027.

## What makes a Halloween saying work on a sign?

A Halloween sign saying is a line brief enough to take in while walking or driving past, lettered big enough for that distance. Unlike a card or caption, strangers read it, often at dusk, from a fixed spot.

The [2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, section 703.5](https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/design-standards/2010-stds/), set 5/8 inch as the minimum character height for an eye-level sign read from under 6 feet, adding 1/8 inch per extra foot. The same section rules out script, italic and "highly decorative" lettering, worth remembering before you pick a dripping-blood font. They bind public buildings, not porches, but make a well-tested benchmark.

## 44 original Halloween sign sayings, grouped by sign type

Each group opens with reading distance, word budget, letter height and material, in that order. Distances are our estimates; measure your own.

### 1. Door hanger sayings (3 to 6 words)

Read from about 3 feet, so 3 to 6 words fit and 5/8-inch capitals are enough. Laminated card or craft foam survives a damp door, hung between 40 and 70 inches up, the band the ADA height rule assumes.

- Coven meeting in progress.
- Shh. The bats are napping.
- Ring once, wake the dead.
- Mummy is resting. Knock gently.
- This door creaks on purpose.
- Guarded by one small werewolf.
- Ghosts inside. Wipe your feet.
- Potion brewing. Please knock twice.

### 2. Porch board sayings (6 to 12 words)

Read from the foot of the steps, roughly 12 feet, so 6 to 12 words is the limit and capitals should be about 1 3/8 inches. A painted plank or chalkboard under the porch roof keeps longer lines dry.

- Welcome, mortals. The pumpkins have been expecting you.
- Mind the steps; the skeletons already tripped on them.
- Each lantern on this porch was carved by a nervous human.
- Come up slowly. Something under the porch is counting.
- Our spiders work nights, so please excuse the webs.
- The ghost who lives here prefers polite visitors.
- Leave your broom by the railing and come say boo.
- Haunted all month, closed for repairs on 1 November.

### 3. Yard sign sayings (2 to 4 big words)

Read from the pavement or a passing car, about 40 feet, so 2 to 4 words in capitals of 4 to 5 inches, never under 1 1/3. Corrugated plastic on a wire stake shrugs off rain.

- GHOSTS CROSSING
- BEWARE OF BATS
- PUMPKIN PATROL ZONE
- ZOMBIES: KEEP OFF GRASS
- RESIDENT WITCH ON DUTY
- BONE YARD
- HAUNTED. OBVIOUSLY.
- FOG AHEAD, WALK SLOWLY

### 4. Chalkboard and letter board sayings (5 to 9 words)

Read from 6 to 10 feet in a window or by the door, so 5 to 9 words work with capitals around an inch. A letter board ships with a fixed set of plastic letters, so count repeats (three E's, two S's) before committing to a line.

- Tonight's special: one fresh fright, served cold.
- Forecast: ghosts after dark, clearing by Sunday.
- Today's spell: be kind, then be spooky.
- Witch hours: dusk until the last pumpkin blinks out.
- Menu: eye of newt, side of goosebumps.
- Days until Halloween: (chalk in the number).

### 5. Candy-bowl "take 2" signs (4 to 9 words)

Read from 2 to 3 feet by a hand already in the bowl, so 5/8-inch letters do, with the number biggest. Tape the card to the rim or fold it into a tent so it cannot blow into the sweets.

- Take two. The skeleton is counting.
- Two each, please. The bowl remembers.
- Take 2 and leave some for the goblins behind you.
- A pair per pumpkin, please.
- Greedy hands get haunted. Two max.
- Two treats, then the lid closes itself.

### 6. Haunted-path warning signs (2 to 5 words)

Read at night from about 20 feet, so 2 to 5 words in capitals near 2 3/8 inches, lit from the front on stakes beside the path. Put real instructions (step, exit, turn) in plain letters on a separate sign.

- TURN BACK WHILE YOU CAN
- LAST CHANCE TO SCREAM
- YOU WERE WARNED. TWICE.
- KEEP TO THE PATH
- THE TREES ARE LISTENING
- QUICKSAND (PROBABLY NOT)
- THE EXIT IS A RUMOUR
- NO GHOST LEFT BEHIND

## Halloween sign letter sizes compared by sign type

The last column uses the ADA step of 1/8 inch per foot, stricter than the highway ratio, because a homemade sign rarely has a road sign's contrast or lighting. Distances are estimates.

| Sign type | Read from (est.) | Word budget | Capital height to aim for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Door hanger or candy-bowl card | 2–3 ft (0.6–0.9 m) | 3–6 words | 5/8 in (16 mm) |
| Chalkboard or letter board | 6–10 ft (2–3 m) | 5–9 words | 5/8–1 1/8 in (16–29 mm) |
| Porch board | 12 ft (3.7 m) | 6–12 words | 1 3/8 in (35 mm) |
| Haunted-path warning | 20 ft (6 m), at night | 2–5 words | 2 3/8 in (60 mm) |
| Yard sign | 40 ft (12 m) | 2–4 words | 4 7/8 in (124 mm); 1 1/3 in absolute floor |

The yard sign needs letters nearly eight times taller than the door hanger, which is why its word budget is smallest.

## Why longer sayings need bigger letters: what vision research says

The [Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (2009 edition, section 2A.13)](https://mutcd.fhwa.dot.gov/htm/2009/part2/part2a.htm) asks for at least 1 inch of letter height per 30 feet and says word messages should be "as brief as possible". It also advises against punctuation, so "HAUNTED. OBVIOUSLY." is a porch joke, not a road sign. An 11th edition has since replaced this text.

That ratio was built for short, familiar words. A [2011 Journal of Vision review by Legge and Bigelow](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC3428264) reports that people read at full speed only when the lowercase x-height spans roughly 0.2 to 2 degrees of visual angle. Our arithmetic turns the lower bound into a 1/2-inch x-height at 12 feet and about 1.7 inches at 40 feet, so a 10-word porch line needs more size than a 2-word yard sign (abstract read, not the full paper).

## Colours that stay readable at night: contrast for Halloween palettes

[WCAG 2.2 (W3C, 12 December 2024)](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) sets 4.5:1 as the minimum contrast for ordinary on-screen text and 3:1 for large text, and publishes the formula. We ran common Halloween pairs through it using standard web colour values; real paint will differ, so treat these as estimates.

- Gold yellow on black: 15.0:1
- Chalk white on dark slate: 8.0:1
- Pumpkin orange on black: 7.8:1
- Lime green on purple: 4.4:1
- Orange on purple: 3.4:1
- Blood red on black: 3.1:1
- White on orange: 2.7:1
- Purple on black: 2.3:1

Red on black and purple on black fall below 4.5:1, so keep them for borders and letter words in orange, yellow or white. Highway manual section 2A.07 says street lighting does not count as lighting a sign, so aim a battery LED spotlight at the face, and use matte paint, since ADA 703.5.1 asks for a non-glare finish.

## Weatherproofing a Halloween sign until 1 November

A sign staked on 17 October faces 15 nights outdoors up to and including Halloween night. Plain card goes soft after one wet evening, so use laminated card, corrugated plastic, painted wood or a covered chalkboard.

Rain rinses chalk away, so chalk lines belong under a roof or behind glass. Seal painted wood with clear matte outdoor varnish before staking, and give a yard sign two stakes, since one turns a 2-foot board into a sail.

## One saying meant for one person: the Halloween pages

Every sign above talks to a street. SubhSandesh's Halloween pages talk to one reader (partner, friend, relative or child), so they cannot show a line to passers-by.

When a saying is really for someone, the [interactive Halloween card that ends with a carved, glowing pumpkin](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is the quick option: around 5 minutes, six photos, your word on the pumpkin. The [cinematic premium Halloween page with your recorded voice](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) is the bigger gesture, around 10 minutes, with a 60-second voice note, twelve photos, an optional unlock time and one reply sent back to you.

Platform-wide, 90.9% of started pages get published and shared. If your porch sign is secretly an invitation to a haunted-path walk, the [invitation page they reply to](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) fits better; send it only to someone likely to welcome it, so a no costs them nothing.

## When a Halloween sign is the wrong choice

A sign is the wrong tool when visitors need instructions rather than atmosphere. A dark route for small children needs a plain "Exit" arrow and a lit step edge first; a joke sign can stand beside those, never in their place.

Rented homes, HOAs and apartment corridors may limit what goes on doors or lawns, so check first. And a greeting page cannot replace a sign: SubhSandesh pages reach one reader at a time, in English only.

## Sources

- US Department of Justice, [2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design](https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/design-standards/2010-stds/), published 15 September 2010 (sections 703.5.1, 703.5.3, 703.5.5).
- Federal Highway Administration, [MUTCD 2009 Edition, Chapter 2A](https://mutcd.fhwa.dot.gov/htm/2009/part2/part2a.htm), 2009 (sections 2A.07, 2A.13).
- Legge and Bigelow, [Does print size matter for reading? A review of findings from vision science and typography](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC3428264), *Journal of Vision*, 9 August 2011 (abstract read).
- W3C, [Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), Recommendation 12 December 2024.

structuralLimitations: SERP: WebSearch (US index) top results were hijacked-subdomain spam (jump.wordstream.com, teamsync.shenkar.ac.il, static.intrafocus.com x5, netbox.point-broadband.com, msoid.icmbio.gov.br) — 9 of 9 weak. DuckDuckGo (lower confidence) showed restoredecorandmore.com (bot wall, snippet only), midgeo.com, routinelyshares.com, etsy.com x2. No page analysed covers letter size, contrast, lighting or materials.

Legge & Bigelow 2011: europepmc.org returned 403 to the fetcher; the abstract was read via the Europe PMC REST API. The 1/2-inch and 1.7-inch x-heights are our arithmetic (distance × tan 0.2°), not figures from the paper.

MUTCD 2009 edition is quoted because its text is open HTML; the post says an 11th edition has replaced it. The ADA 2010 Standards bind public buildings, not homes — the post says so and uses them as a benchmark only.

Contrast ratios are computed from the WCAG formula using standard web hex values (e.g. #FF7518 pumpkin, #FFD700 gold, #6A0DAD purple, #B22222 firebrick, #2F4F4F slate); paint colours will differ. WCAG is a screen standard, labelled as such.
Sign-industry legibility index (usscfoundation.org) returned 403 and is not cited. Reading distances per sign type are labelled estimates.
